newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED RELIEVED TO GET PAST PLUCKY SPURS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED RELIEVED TO GET PAST PLUCKY SPURS.

text.p: Holders Manchester United maintained their grip on the F.A. Cup when they overcame an injury-ravaged but stubborn Tottenham side 2-0 in a hard-fought third-round tie on Sunday.

The match, between the two most successful clubs in the competition's history with United having won it a record nine times and Spurs eight, went United's way thanks to goals from Paul Scholes after 50 minutes and David Beckham, direct from a 25-metre free kick, 10 minutes from time.

United manager Alex Ferguson praised Tottenham afterwards, saying: "They did really well considering their injuries. Even when we scored they kept at it, kept coming forward. It was a good, hard cup tie and I am glad to have got through it.
"Roy Keane was the man of the match for me. His performance was on a different planet. There is not a player who comes within a thousand of miles of him. He was outstanding."

Tottenham, heavily criticised after their 7-1 defeat at Newcastle on December 28, played without six first team regulars including strikers Teddy Sheringham, Steffen Iversen and Chris Armstrong and defender John Scales -- as well as long-term injuries Gary Mabbutt and Darren Anderton.

Manager Gerry Francis was forced to play two 19-year-olds in attack, debutant Neale Fenn and Rory Allen, who has made just eight starts for Spurs, and was full of praise for his team despite their defeat.

"I thought we did really well and did not deserve to lose," he said. "The players who played today did the club proud. It is hard enough coming here with a full squad, but is even harder with half the first team missing.
"We had a great opportunity to level after they scored, but there was not much we could do about the free kick, it was a world class strike.
"I think Alex will be very relieved that they won the game. We limited them to very little, but it hurts being out of the F.A. Cup."

Despite their handicaps, Spurs had the better of the first half, with Andy Sinton helping them dominate the midfield and with a little more experience in attack, could have severely embarrased the home side.

United went ahead when Scholes beat Walker with a well-placed shot from 15-metres after good approach work by Andy Cole, making his first start for United since last season's Cup Final, and Beckham, who made the final pass.
Beckham, a Londonder who trained with Spurs as a youngester, then killed them off with his free-kick that flew over the Spurs wall and gave Walker no chance.
There were near-misses by both sides -- Walker denying Giggs with a point-blank header after 26 minutes and Scholes a second goal with an acrobatic save in the dying minutes.

United's French skipper Eric Cantona, who has never been on the losing side in an F.A. Cup tie in five seasons in England at Leeds and United, had a poor match, but also went close near the end with a lobbed shot that bounced just wide.
Tottenham's best chance fell to Allen a minute after United scored, but, stretching at the far post, he sent the ball wide.

As far as Tottenham are concerned the defeat effectively ends their season. They are well off the pace for the title and already out of the League Cup. The best they can hope for is to finish high enough in the league and gain a UEFA Cup place next season.
United, with five clean sheets behind them, never approached their best on Sunday but are hard to beat and well placed in the title race as well as being in the quarter-finals of the European Cup.

They face either Crewe or Wimbledon in the fourth round as they continue their bid to become the first club ever to reach four successive Cup Finals. If they do, they will not want too many matches as hard as this one on the way to Wembley.
Teams:

Manchester United - 1-Peter Schmeichel, 2-Gary Neville, 3-Denis Irwin (13-Brian McClair 52), 4-David May, 19-Ronny Johnsen, 16-Roy Keane, 7-Eric Cantona, 10-David Beckham, 11-Ryan Giggs, 9-Andy Cole (20-Ole Solksjaer 79), 18-Paul Scholes

Tottenham Hotspur - 1-Ian Walker, 2-Dean Austin, 3-Justin Edinburgh, 25-Stephen Carr, 23-Sol Campbell, 5-Colin Calderwood, 4-David Howells, 8-Allan Nielsen, 27-Andy Sinton, 20-Neale Fenn, 29-Rory Allen
